trend.note: Monthly counts of police-reported cyclist crashes citywide since Sept 2017; ksi = crashes whose worst injury was fatal or incapacitating ("killed or seriously injured"). Recent months are provisional — records get amended.

findings.title: Cyclists killed or seriously injured
findings.description: A cyclist was killed or seriously injured ("incapacitating" in police records) in 7 crashes in the 12 months through 2026-06-28, vs 10 the prior 12 months. Vision Zero's goal is zero.
findings.caveat: Counts, not rates — ridership growth is not netted out. Recent months are provisional.

findings.title: How much of the network protects riders
findings.description: Only 20% of Chicago's 65 on-street bikeway miles are physically protected lanes (13 mi); counting buffered lanes brings it to 38%. The rest is paint, sharrows, and greenways. Off-street trails are tracked separately.
findings.caveat: Share of current on-street network mileage as of 2026-07-14; protected = barrier/curb-protected on-street lanes. Off-street trails are excluded — they live in the separate OSM layer.

findings.title: How much of the street grid has bike infrastructure
findings.description: Chicago has 655 miles of surface streets (arterials, collectors, and neighborhood streets). 65 miles — 10% — have any bike infrastructure at all, counting everything from sharrows to protected lanes.
findings.caveat: Centerline miles on both sides of the ratio. Expressways, ramps, alleys, and river channels are excluded from street miles; off-street trails are excluded from bikeway miles. The street centerline layer was last updated in 2021 — the grid changes slowly.

findings.title: Highest crash-density corridors
findings.description: Top corridors by cyclist crashes per km of bikeway: Kinzie St (19.28/km); Dearborn St (17.11/km); Stony Island Ave (10.81/km); Wood St (9.83/km); Augusta Blvd (8.89/km).
findings.caveat: Raw counts, not normalized by bike volume. Dooring is undercounted. Per-km rates inflate short segments — Kinzie's rate rides on very few km.

findings.title: How often the driver leaves
findings.description: In 13% of police-reported cyclist crashes since Sept 2017 (161 of 1200), the driver left the scene — 14% when the cyclist was injured.
findings.caveat: Share of reported crashes; unreported crashes are not counted.

findings.title: Ward concentration
findings.description: 5 of 50 wards account for 47% of located cyclist crashes since Sept 2017: Ward 33 (180), Ward 38 (132), Ward 34 (116), Ward 39 (76), Ward 23 (61).
findings.caveat: Ward totals reflect where people ride most, not only where streets are worst.

findings.title: Dooring: structurally undercounted
findings.description: 63 crashes since Sept 2017 carry a dooring flag. Dooring is structurally excluded from 'reportable' crash records unless damage/injury thresholds are met, so the real number is higher than any count on this site.
findings.caveat: A floor, not a full count.

findings.title: How Chicago's bike network scores nationally
findings.description: PeopleForBikes' Bicycle Network Analysis scores how much of Chicago a person can reach on low-stress streets — and gives the city 11.08 out of 100. The average rated U.S. city scores 24. Among the 2 rated U.S. cities over 300,000 people, Chicago ranks last. Behind the number: 6,267 miles of high-stress streets versus 1,834 low-stress. That's up slightly from 9 in 2025. This grades the network, not crashes: it can move independently of any crash trend, because it measures what's built, not what happened.
findings.caveat: Third-party score, analysis 26.05 (May 2026). Computed by PeopleForBikes from OpenStreetMap — only as current as volunteer mapping, which is uneven across neighborhoods; it can understate what a neighborhood has, or miss hazards nobody mapped. PFB's scoring methodology has changed over the years (notably 2020 and 2026), so history entries are not comparable across distant analysis versions. It grades the street network, not the people riding it — a low score is a case for building more, not a reason not to ride.

bikeway_mileage.note: Citywide bikeway miles by facility type across 2 snapshots (2025-01-15 to 2026-07-12). Miles use CDOT centerline mileage where available, else projected geometry length. The CDOT Bike Routes layer has no install-date field, so this series is built forward from snapshots.

protected_share.note: Protected share of on-street bikeway miles; excludes off-street trails.
